slides.title: Side hustle taxes: the $400 rule
slides.sub: Make $400 or more in profit and you owe self-employment tax.

slides.heading: The $400 rule
body: If your net earnings from self-employment are $400 or more in a year, you owe self-employment tax and need to file a tax return. There's no age exception.
Net earnings means what you made minus business costs, like supplies or equipment.

slides.heading: What you pay
body: It's Social Security (12.4%) and Medicare (2.9%). At a regular job you pay half and your employer pays half. Self-employed, you pay both.
Example: $3,000 of profit detailing cars means about $424 in self-employment tax (figured on 92.35% of profit).

slides.heading: No 1099? Still taxable
body: Starting with 2026, businesses only have to send a 1099-NEC once they pay you $2,000 or more. Payment apps send a 1099-K after $20,000 and 200 transactions.
No form doesn't mean no tax. Track every payment and expense in a simple spreadsheet.
slides.source: One Big Beautiful Bill Act, via CPA Practice Advisor

slides.takeaway: Set aside part of every side hustle payment for taxes, and keep your receipts.

posts.caption:
Got a side hustle? Detailing cars, mowing lawns, reselling sneakers, tutoring? Here's the tax rule most teens miss.

If your net earnings from self-employment are $400 or more, you owe self-employment tax (IRS). Net earnings means what you made minus business costs like supplies. The tax is 15.3%: 12.4% for Social Security and 2.9% for Medicare. At a job your employer pays half; self-employed, you pay both. Example: $3,000 of profit means about $424 in self-employment tax (figured on 92.35% of profit).

New for 2026: businesses only have to send you a 1099-NEC once they pay you $2,000 or more, and payment apps send a 1099-K after $20,000 and 200 transactions. The income is still taxable either way, so track every payment and expense.

Data: IRS self-employment tax page (updated Oct. 30, 2026); 1099 changes in the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (CPA Practice Advisor).
